name: Advertising ID (IDFA and AAID)
plain: A resettable ad ID: Android gives it by default, iOS only after the person taps Allow in the ATT prompt.
meaning: The cross-app profile key for ad targeting. ATT (iOS 14.5) cut iOS opt-in to roughly 25 percent in industry surveys; Android lets users delete it in Settings.

android.revocation: Settings > Privacy > Ads > Delete advertising ID
android.store_policy: Play: ad ID banned in children's apps
android.note: UUID; zeroed after opt-out or delete (Android 12)

limits.headline: Can use a resettable ad ID, by default on Android and only after Allow on iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing on Android. On iPhone you tap Allow on the tracking prompt
can: Join your activity across apps for ad targeting
Keep the same ID until you reset or delete it
Give zeros after you delete it (Android 12 and later) or refuse tracking (iPhone)
cannot: Get the real ID on iPhone after you tap Ask App Not to Track
Keep the ID after you delete it on Android
Skip the iPhone prompt, where only about 25 percent say yes, by industry surveys
limits.differs: Android gives the ad ID by default and lets you delete it. iPhone gives it only after you tap Allow.

story.what_it_is: A resettable ad ID: Android gives it freely, and iOS only after you tap Allow.

marketing.name: App Tracking Transparency and IDFA
marketing.pitch: Apps need permission before they can use the advertising identifier.

marketing.name: Advertising ID
marketing.pitch: A user resettable, unique ID for advertising purposes on Android.

story.for_you: On Android it is on by default, and you can reset or delete it. On iPhone an app has to ask first, and a no returns zeros.
story.for_makers: It is the cross app profile key for ad targeting. ATT cut iOS opt in to roughly 25 percent in industry surveys, while Android users can delete it but rarely do.

use_cases.example: An ad network shows you a banner for a hotel after you searched travel in another app.
A game credits an install to a rewarded ad and grants a bonus.
A retailer builds an audience of past buyers to show loyalty ads.
A growth team measures how many installs came from each network.
A fraud tool flags one ID with dozens of installs in a minute.
A kids game must not send the ID at all.

story.android_note: Android: the Google advertising ID, on by default with delete or reset in settings.
story.ios_note: iOS: the IDFA, available only after you tap Allow on the ATT prompt.

history.change: Ad ID zeroed on opt-out or delete
